rationale: The question is how well a code (the index test) agrees with laboratory-defined disease (the reference standard), which is a diagnostic accuracy question answered by a cross-sectional sample of registered adults. Counting uncoded patients alone would give sensitivity but not the positive predictive value that the recoding decision also needs. The recorded search returned nothing, so no claim is cited; the design rests on the confirmed empty search and the investigator's local facts.
alternatives: Cross-sectional count of uncoded patients only (refused: says nothing about wrong codes)
Recoding exercise without measurement (refused: could add doubtful codes, as incentive-driven registers did)
Manual review of every record (refused: outside the 60-hour allowance; a random sample is reviewed instead)
whyNotMoreComplex: A prospective study with repeat testing would reduce partial verification but needs patient contact, which the constraints exclude; existing records answer the decision question.

decision.statement: Narrow the question to the sensitivity and positive predictive value of kidney disease stage 3 to 5 codes against laboratory-defined disease in the six practices' existing records, and decide on recoding only after the estimate.
decision.question: How should the network find out whether its kidney disease codes are accurate enough before funding recoding?

criteria.text: Most adults with laboratory-defined disease have at least two eGFR results in the window, so the reference standard can be applied.
A network-wide validation using the same laboratory data already exists.

gates.requirement: Approval for a pseudonymised extract of codes and laboratory results from all six practices
gates.evidence: Data protection officer approval DPA-PCN-2026-14 dated 3 September 2026, supplied by the investigator
Service evaluation classification SE-PCN-2026-03 dated 10 September 2026, supplied by the investigator

decision.note: No ledger claim exists because the recorded search returned no records; the decision rests on the confirmed empty search and the investigator's approvals.

summary: Diagnostic accuracy design recommended; the decision narrows the question, cites no claim and has both gates met.
